title: Qualify canonical host and signed guest runtime mailbox compatibility
body:
Parents: #43 / #42. Platform qualification: #46. Observed while qualifying original collector ownership in #111.

Native trial 12 at contributor MVM `61f727164` and SpiralCore `a2513cfb` starts both installed Linux/Firecracker guests, passes strict original-owner entrypoint admission and cleanly retires both original helpers/collectors. The source workload exits 1. Its console independently reports a mailbox boot-file refusal: generated source boot 2553 bytes; exact verified signed runtime candidate source `ffd90f895d7080629eceb16095d1ca81c0a49b95` permits 2048 bytes, whereas current host source permits 8192. Original helper meter shows failed write and 0 accepted application bytes. Workload stderr was not included in the terminal error, so console and exit remain separate observations. No positive transfer claim.

The inspected latest upstream release workflow [43486823143](https://github.com/tinylabscom/mvm/actions/runs/43486823143) is the rc.3 candidate used here. Newer source-build releases inspected contain host helpers, not a compatible signed guest runtime. Artifact signature verification does not prove host/guest semantic compatibility.

- [ ] State exact supported host/guest runtime revisions and their canonical mailbox/control/boot contract compatibility.
- [ ] Obtain or produce through the canonical authorized publication process a compatible verified runtime. No in-place signed archive patch, fabricated official identity, signature bypass or guest-bound waiver.
- [x] Add canonical pre-dispatch compatibility refusal using the existing runtime ownership/metadata route; do not introduce a competing SpiralCore guest-runtime authority or infer capabilities from version labels alone.
- [ ] Preserve the old runtime/oversized boot failure as a regression; ensure incompatible selection refuses before readiness or application effects.
- [ ] Rerun actual two-guest exact delivery+ACK+independent readback and original-owner retirement. Record actual bidirectional traffic, CPU, wall time, all source/artifact identities and retained resource state.
- [ ] Keep installed Linux success distinct from remaining macOS/Windows roles, cross-host WAN, recovery and release qualification.

Evidence: [native lifecycle report](https://github.com/R4-Laboratories/SpiralCore/blob/codex/owned-journal-admission-results/docs/network/evidence/2026-11-14-owned-collector/native-journal.md). This gate does not negate the positive original-owner retirement result; it blocks complete current-source application-transfer acceptance.


Host implementation and executed checks: [PR #271](https://github.com/R4-Laboratories/SpiralCore/pull/271). This checks only the implemented pre-dispatch refusal; compatible signed runtime and positive native acceptance remain open.
